T: Every father wants better for his son.
D: A mob enforcer and his son go on the run across Depression-era Illinois.
P: Serve dessert at the diner stop on the road to Perdition.
S: Diner grilled cheese with quick pickles
the roadside diners across Illinois where Sullivan and his son stop

Sharp cheddar grilled cheese fried in butter until crisp, cut into fingers and served with sweet dill bread-and-butter pickles. Thinly slice 2 Lebanese cucumbers and 1 small onion. Heat 150ml white vinegar, 100ml water, 60g sugar, 1 tsp salt and 1 tsp mustard seeds until dissolved, pour over and cool for 30 minutes. Butter 8 slices white bread on the outside, fill with 200g sliced cheddar and fry over medium heat for 3 minutes a side until golden. Cut into fingers and serve with the pickles.
the old couple who take them in
Rye sourdough warmed at 180C for 8 minutes, salted butter and apple butter (apples cooked down slowly with cider and cinnamon).
Warm Irish soda bread with a craggy crust, torn and served with salted butter and sharp cheddar.
M: Slow-simmered corned beef sliced thick with buttery cabbage, carrots and potatoes and hot mustard. Simmer a 1.5kg corned silverside with an onion, 2 bay leaves and 6 peppercorns for 2.5 hours.
the diner stops on the run
Poach chicken thighs, make a velouté with the stock, butter and flour, add peas, carrot and thyme, top with puff pastry, bake at 200C for 25 minutes.
W: farmhouse style, like the old couple would serve
Deep-dish apple pie with a slice of sharp cheddar melted on top in the last 5 minutes.
K: the Rooney wake, 1931, whiskey poured freely for the dead

Hot strong coffee with Irish whiskey and brown sugar, under a thick collar of lightly whipped cream. Whip 150ml thickened cream to soft ribbons, so it just holds its shape. Brew 600ml strong coffee. Warm 4 heatproof glasses with hot water and tip it out. Add 2 tsp brown sugar and 40ml Irish whiskey to each glass, then 150ml coffee, and stir until dissolved. Pour the cream gently over the back of a spoon to float on top. Do not stir.

dishes.n: Diner grilled cheese with quick pickles
dishes.make_ahead: Pickles up to 1 week ahead, keep chilled

steps.text: Thinly slice the cucumbers and onion.
Heat the vinegar, water, sugar, salt and mustard seeds until dissolved, then pour over the vegetables.
Let the pickles cool and sit while you make the sandwiches.
Butter the bread on the outside and fill with the cheddar.
Fry over medium heat until golden on both sides. Cut into fingers and serve with the pickles.

dishes.make_ahead: Best the day it is baked

steps.text: Mix the flour, bicarbonate of soda and salt, add the buttermilk and bring together into a round. Cut a deep cross on top.
Bake at 220C.
Reduce the oven to 200C and bake until golden and hollow when tapped. Serve warm with the butter and cheddar.

dishes.make_ahead: Beef can be cooked 1 day ahead, keep chilled in its liquid

steps.text: Peel the onion, potatoes and carrots and cut the potatoes and carrots into chunks. Quarter the cabbage.
Cover the corned silverside with water in a large pot with the onion, bay leaves and peppercorns and bring to a gentle simmer.
Simmer the corned silverside gently, topping up the water as needed.
Add the potatoes and carrots and keep simmering.
Add the cabbage for the last of the cooking.
Slice the corned silverside thick and serve with the vegetables, butter and mustard.

veg.make_ahead: Celeriac can be simmered 1 day ahead, keep chilled in its liquid

steps.text: Peel the onion, celeriacs, potatoes and carrots. Cut each celeriac into 4 thick slabs, cut the potatoes and carrots into chunks and quarter the cabbage.
Fill a large pot with water and add the onion, bay leaves, peppercorns, cloves, brown sugar, malt vinegar and salt. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the celeriac and simmer gently.
Add the potatoes and carrots and keep simmering, adding the cabbage for the last 10 minutes.
Melt half the butter, stir in the flour, whisk in the milk and simmer until thick. Stir in the parsley.
Lift out the celeriac and brown it in the rest of the butter in a hot pan.
Serve the celeriac with the vegetables, parsley sauce and mustard.

dishes.make_ahead: Up to 1 day ahead, reheat to serve

steps.text: Peel, core and slice the apples. Cook them gently with the sugar and cinnamon for 5 minutes, then cool.
Line a deep pie dish with one pastry sheet, fill with the apples, cover with the second sheet and cut slits in the top.
Bake at 190C until golden.
Lay the cheddar on top for the last stretch of baking so it melts.

dishes.make_ahead: Whip the cream up to 2 hours ahead, keep chilled

steps.text: Whip the cream to soft ribbons so it just holds its shape. Brew the coffee.
Warm 4 heatproof glasses with hot water and tip it out.
Add brown sugar, whiskey and coffee to each glass and stir until dissolved.
Float the cream on top over the back of a spoon. Do not stir.

af.make_ahead: Whip the cream up to 2 hours ahead, keep chilled

steps.text: Whip the cream to soft ribbons so it just holds its shape. Brew the coffee.
Warm 4 heatproof glasses with hot water and tip it out.
Add brown sugar, a few drops of vanilla and coffee to each glass and stir until dissolved.
Float the cream on top over the back of a spoon. Do not stir.

s.n: Diner grilled cheese with quick pickles
s.note: Sharp cheddar grilled cheese fried in butter until crisp, cut into fingers and served with sweet dill bread-and-butter pickles.
s.how: Thinly slice 2 Lebanese cucumbers and 1 small onion. Heat 150ml white vinegar, 100ml water, 60g sugar, 1 tsp salt and 1 tsp mustard seeds until dissolved, pour over and cool for 30 minutes. Butter 8 slices white bread on the outside, fill with 200g sliced cheddar and fry over medium heat for 3 minutes a side until golden. Cut into fingers and serve with the pickles.

Mix 450g plain flour, 1 tsp bicarb soda and 1 tsp salt, add 400ml buttermilk and bring together into a round. Cut a deep cross on top and bake at 220C for 15 minutes, then 200C for 25 minutes. Serve warm with 100g salted butter and 200g sharp cheddar.

m.how: Simmer a 1.5kg corned silverside with an onion, 2 bay leaves and 6 peppercorns for 2.5 hours. Add 600g potatoes and 3 carrots for the last 30 minutes and a quartered cabbage for the last 10. Slice the beef thick and serve with the veg, butter and hot English mustard.

w.note: farmhouse style, like the old couple would serve
w.how: Peel and slice 1kg Granny Smith apples, cook 5 minutes with 80g sugar and 1 tsp cinnamon, and cool. Line a deep pie dish with 1 sheet sweet shortcrust, fill, cover with a second sheet and cut slits. Bake at 190C for 45 minutes. Lay 120g sliced sharp cheddar on top for the last 5 minutes so it melts.
